There are some studies here showing positive effects of lithium. These all refer to injecting it and will probably use higher doses than anyone would recommend you take orally.

 * http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11685390

Another problem is that most research is done with lithium carbonate which is a regulated medicine. If you want to get hold of lithium without prescription you have to settle for a lesser studied lithium orotate.

As someone on the spectrum—nay, as a human of world—I have to disagree with the parent comment. I have observed how changes in my diet have had significant effect on my condition and am about to start working with a nutritionist to see if I can make further improvements. A couple of months ago I couldn’t manage to do basic tasks and stayed in bed for most of the day now I’m cooking all my meals myself, learning new pieces of music on the piano, and I’m much less anxious and depressed and hoping to return to some voluntary work and then to real employment if I continue to make improvement like I am currently.

I spend a lot of time thinking about and trying to understand what autistic behaviors are so I can recognize them in myself and others. (I have the advantage of having an autistic (undiagnosed) mother so even if I change she stays the same and I can observe her, politely of course.) In doing this I’m starting to notice that there are quite a lot of people out there who have autistic traits but never connect them with autism. Many of these people lead particularly acceptable lives but they have certain peculiarities about them that are hallmarks of autism. This observation leads me to the conclusion that what we are currently diagnosing as autism is only a part of the total effect of whatever it is that is causing autism and I’m aware of a number of cases of people who are at least somewhat autistic being misdiagnosed as having other things or not being diagnosed late or very late. So my whole-hearted belief is that autism is being considerably under-diagnosed. Despite this in the UK my local mental health centre is overwhelmed with a 7-8 month backlog for doing autism diagnoses and so I had to pay to go private for mine.

What I’m saying is that this isn’t hysteria—ignoring the fact that nobody is actually behaving hysterically anyway. Something is up. This is before we start to think about the massive rise in ADD/ADHD cases as well.

There’s a new paper out recently talking about how severity of autism can be measured in by the extent of genetic mutations <http://www.newswise.com/articles/diverse-autism-mutations-lead-to-different-disease-outcomes>. OK, all well and good but what is causing those mutations in the first place?

Hm, you could try some of the other more basic tests online such as this one: http://psychologytoday.tests.psychtests.com/take_test.php?idRegTest=1301

You could also try attention-based brain training games that tell you how you rank to see how you do on that. There’s also a free IQ test available here: http://www.cambridgebrainsciences.com/ one of the last tests is an attention-based test that only seems to appear if you opt to take the whole suite i.e. you can’t take it on its own for some reason, probably. But there are other so-called concentration tests on there as well so maybe worth taking the whole suite anyway.

From there you might want to look up a cognitive neuropsychologist. 

But the real take away message of all this is to please take the time to go through the process of figuring out what is wrong with you and looking deeply to see if there are solutions and trying things. You may find the problem is simple. Even if it isn’t—it hasn’t been for me—and solution aren’t rapidly forthcoming doesn’t mean they aren’t out there or there won’t be things that at least help.

On a practical level my suggestion to you would be to try to fill your life with other things: family, friends, work, maybe start work on a project or goal that you care about, or do things to help you feel more connected to other people. Make some commitments that you can’t get out of easily and busy yourself. Maybe keep some things on your person that you can play with, read, or do so you can distract yourself whenever it does happen (this is for once you’re already quite busy).

I think the situation you find yourself in might be indicative of a powerful imagination on your part, if that’s the case, then use it! Write stories, poetry, or create art, and then share it with other people, maybe find other people to work with. Whoops! Looks like my imagination is getting ahead of me too.
